questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
Mass of substance		List-II
Number of atoms
A. $1.8$ mg waterI. $2\times 10^{-4}\times N_A$
B. $9.8$ mg sulphuric acidII. $1.5\times 10^{-4}\times N_A$
C. $1.8$ mg carbonIII. $3\times 10^{-4}\times N_A$
D. $5.85$ mg salt (NaCl)IV. $7\times 10^{-4}\times N_A$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For A: Molar mass of $H_2O = 18$ g/mol. Moles of $H_2O = \dfrac{1.8 \times 10^{-3}}{18} = 10^{-4}$. Since each $H_2O$ molecule has $3$ atoms, the number of atoms = $3 \times 10^{-4} \times N_A$.

For B: Molar mass of $H_2SO_4 = 98$ g/mol. Moles of $H_2SO_4 = \dfrac{9.8 \times 10^{-3}}{98} = 10^{-4}$. Since each $H_2SO_4$ molecule has $7$ atoms, the number of atoms = $7 \times 10^{-4} \times N_A$.

For C: Molar mass of $C = 12$ g/mol. Moles of $C = \dfrac{1.8 \times 10^{-3}}{12} = 1.5 \times 10^{-4}$. The number of atoms = $1.5 \times 10^{-4} \times N_A$.

For D: Molar mass of $NaCl = 58.5$ g/mol. Moles of $NaCl = \dfrac{5.85 \times 10^{-3}}{58.5} = 10^{-4}$. Since each $NaCl$ formula unit has $2$ atoms, the number of atoms = $2 \times 10^{-4} \times N_A$.

Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following contain the same number of atoms ? (Given : Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of H, He, O and S are $1, 4, 16$ and $32$ respectively)
A. $2$ g of O_2$ gas \\ B. $4$ g of SO_2$ gas
C. $1400$ mL of O_2$ at STP \\ D. $0.05$ L of He at STP \\ E. $0.0625$ mol of H_2$ gas
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Number of atoms is calculated as the product of the number of moles, atomicity, and Avogadro's number ($N_A$).

For A: Moles of O_2$ = $\dfrac{2}{32} = \dfrac{1}{16}$ mol. Atomicity of O_2$ is $2$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{16} \times 2 \times N_A = \dfrac{1}{8} N_A$

For B: Moles of SO_2$ = $\dfrac{4}{64} = \dfrac{1}{16}$ mol. Atomicity of SO_2$ is $3$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{16} \times 3 \times N_A = \dfrac{3}{16} N_A$

For C: Moles of O_2$ at STP = $\dfrac{1400}{22400} = \dfrac{1}{16}$ mol. Atomicity of O_2$ is $2$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{16} \times 2 \times N_A = \dfrac{1}{8} N_A$

For D: Moles of He at STP = $\dfrac{0.05}{22.4} = \dfrac{1}{448}$ mol. Atomicity of He is $1$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{448} \times 1 \times N_A = \dfrac{1}{448} N_A$

For E: Moles of H_2$ = $0.0625 = \dfrac{1}{16}$ mol. Atomicity of H_2$ is $2$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{16} \times 2 \times N_A = \dfrac{1}{8} N_A$

Comparing the number of atoms, A, C, and E contain the same number of atoms.

Answer: A, C and E only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An oxide of iron contains $69.9\%$ iron, its empirical formula, is: (Given: Molar mass of Fe and O are $56$ and $16$ g mol$^{-1}$ respectively.)
questions.solution:
Mass percentage of $\text{Fe} = 69.9\%$

Mass percentage of $\text{O} = 100\% - 69.9\% = 30.1\%$

Number of moles of $\text{Fe} = \dfrac{69.9}{56} = 1.248$

Number of moles of $\text{O} = \dfrac{30.1}{16} = 1.881$

Molar ratio of $\text{Fe} : \text{O} = 1.248 : 1.881$

Dividing by the smallest value, the ratio is $\dfrac{1.248}{1.248} : \dfrac{1.881}{1.248} = 1 : 1.5$

Multiplying by $2$ to get the simplest whole number ratio, we get $2 : 3$.

The empirical formula is $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$.

Answer: $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What volume of hydrogen gas at STP would be liberated by action of $50\text{ mL}$ of $H_2SO_4$ of $50\%$ purity (density $= 1.3\text{ g mL}^{-1}$) on $20\text{ g}$ of zinc ?
Given : Molar mass of H, O, S, Zn are $1, 16, 32, 65\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ respectively.
questions.solution:
Mass of $H_2SO_4$ solution $= 50 \times 1.3 = 65\text{ g}$

Mass of pure $H_2SO_4 = 65 \times \dfrac{50}{100} = 32.5\text{ g}$

Moles of $H_2SO_4 = \dfrac{32.5}{98} \approx 0.3316\text{ mol}$

Moles of $Zn = \dfrac{20}{65} \approx 0.3077\text{ mol}$

The balanced chemical equation is:
$Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2$

Since the moles of $Zn$ are less than the moles of $H_2SO_4$, $Zn$ is the limiting reagent.

Moles of $H_2$ produced $=$ Moles of $Zn = \dfrac{20}{65}\text{ mol}$

Volume of $H_2$ gas at STP $= \dfrac{20}{65} \times 22.4\text{ L} = 6.892\text{ L}$

Answer: $6.892\text{ L}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
How many grams of residue is obtained by heating $2.76$ g of silver carbonate?
(Given: Molar mass of C, O and Ag are $12$, $16$ and $108$ g mol$^{-1}$ respectively)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $Ag_2CO_3$ = $2 \times 108 + 12 + 3 \times 16 = 276$ g mol$^{-1}$

Number of moles of $Ag_2CO_3$ = $\dfrac{2.76}{276} = 0.01$ mol

The decomposition reaction of silver carbonate on heating is:

$Ag_2CO_3(s) \rightarrow 2Ag(s) + CO_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}O_2(g)$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1$ mole of $Ag_2CO_3$ gives $2$ moles of Ag as residue.

Number of moles of Ag formed = $2 \times 0.01 = 0.02$ mol

Mass of Ag residue = $0.02 \times 108 = 2.16$ g

Answer: $2.16$ g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The correct order of total number of atoms present in
(A) $2$ moles of cyclohexane
(B) $684$ g of sucrose
(C) $90.8$ L of dihydrogen at STP
is:
questions.solution:
For (A):

Formula of cyclohexane is $C_6H_{12}$.

Number of atoms per molecule = $6 + 12 = 18$.

Total number of atoms in $2$ moles = $2 \times 18 \times N_A = 36 N_A$.

For (B):

Formula of sucrose is $C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}$.

Molar mass of sucrose = $342$ g/mol.

Number of moles = $\dfrac{684}{342} = 2$ moles.

Number of atoms per molecule = $12 + 22 + 11 = 45$.

Total number of atoms = $2 \times 45 \times N_A = 90 N_A$.

For (C):

Formula of dihydrogen is $H_2$.

Number of moles at STP = $\dfrac{90.8}{22.7} = 4$ moles.

Number of atoms per molecule = $2$.

Total number of atoms = $4 \times 2 \times N_A = 8 N_A$.

Comparing the total number of atoms:

$90 N_A \gt 36 N_A \gt 8 N_A$

Therefore, the correct order is $B \gt A \gt C$.

Answer: $B\gt A\gt C$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Number of moles and number of molecules in $1.4187$ L of $SO_2$ at STP respectively are:
questions.solution:
Volume of $SO_2$ at STP $= 1.4187$ L

Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP is approximately $22.414$ L.

Number of moles $n = \dfrac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Molar Volume}} = \dfrac{1.4187}{22.414} = 0.0633$

Number of molecules $= n \times N_A$

Number of molecules $= 0.0633 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 3.812 \times 10^{22}$

Answer: $0.0633; 3.812 \times 10^{22}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ratio of mass percentage (w/w) of C : H in a hydrocarbon is $12 : 1$. It has two carbon atoms. The weight (in g) of $CO_2(g)$ formed when $3.38$ g of this hydrocarbon is completely burnt in oxygen is : (Given : Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, O : 16)
questions.solution:
Ratio of mass percentage of C : H = $12 : 1$

Ratio of moles of C : H = $\dfrac{12}{12} : \dfrac{1}{1} = 1 : 1$

The empirical formula is $CH$. Since the hydrocarbon has two carbon atoms, its molecular formula is $C_2H_2$.

Molar mass of $C_2H_2 = 2 \times 12 + 2 \times 1 = 26$ g mol$^{-1}$

Moles of $C_2H_2$ in $3.38$ g = $\dfrac{3.38}{26} = 0.13$ mol

The combustion reaction is:

$C_2H_2 + \dfrac{5}{2}O_2 \rightarrow 2CO_2 + H_2O$

From the stoichiometry, $1$ mole of $C_2H_2$ produces $2$ moles of $CO_2$.

Moles of $CO_2$ produced = $2 \times 0.13 = 0.26$ mol

Molar mass of $CO_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44$ g mol$^{-1}$

Weight of $CO_2$ formed = $0.26 \times 44 = 11.44$ g

Answer: $11.44$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the given reaction:
$\mathrm{CaCO}_{3}+2 \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaCl}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_{2}$
If $90 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{CaCO}_{3}$ is added to 300 mL of HCl which contains $38.55 \% \mathrm{HCl}$ by mass and has density $1.13 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}$, then which of the following option is correct ?
Given molar mass of $\mathrm{H}, \mathrm{Cl}, \mathrm{Ca}$ and O are 1, 35.5, 40 and $16 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively.
questions.solution:
Molar masses: HCl = 36.5, CaCO₃ = 100 g/mol
HCl solution: mass = 300 × 1.13 = 339 g
HCl present: 339 × 0.3855 = 130.74 g = 130.74/36.5 = 3.58 mol
CaCO₃: 90/100 = 0.9 mol
Reaction: $CaCO_3 + 2HCl → CaCl_2 + H_2O + CO_2$
HCl required: 0.9 × 2 = 1.8 mol
HCl available: 3.58 mol > 1.8 mol
CaCO₃ is limiting. HCl remaining: (3.58 - 1.8) × 36.5 = 1.78 × 36.5 = 64.97 g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$\mathrm{A}+2 \mathrm{~B} \longrightarrow \mathrm{AB}_{2}$
36.0 g of 'A' (Molar mass: $60 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$) and 56.0 g of ' $\mathrm{B}^{\prime}$ (Molar mass: $80 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$) are allowed to react. Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. 'A' is the limiting reagent.
B. $77.0 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$ is formed.
C. Molar mass of $A B_{2}$ is $140 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$.
D. $15.0 \mathrm{~g}$ of A is left unreacted after the completion of reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Reaction: A + 2B → AB₂.
Moles of A = 36.0/60 = 0.6 mol;
Moles of B = 56.0/80 = 0.7 mol.
A requires 1.2 mol of B but only 0.7 available, so B is limiting reagent.
So, (A) False - B is limiting.
(B) AB₂ formed = 0.7/2 = 0.35 mol;
Molar mass AB₂ = 60 + 2(80) = 220 g/mol;
Mass = 0.35 × 220 = 77 g True.
(C) False - Molar mass is 220 g/mol.
(D) A remaining = 0.6 - 0.35 = 0.25 mol = 15 g True.
Correct statements: B and D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the reaction,
$2 \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s})+6 \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Al}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq})+6 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+3 \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$
options: $11.2 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ at STP is produced for every mole of HCl consumed.
$33.6 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ is produced regardless of temperature and pressure for every mole of Al that reacts.
$67.2 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ at STP is produced for every mole of Al that reacts.
questions.solution:
Reaction: $2\text{Al}(s) + 6\text{HCl}(aq) \rightarrow 2\text{Al}^{3+}(aq) + 6\text{Cl}^-(aq) + 3\text{H}_2(g)$
Checking each option:
(1) Per 1 mole HCl: From stoichiometry, 6 mol HCl produces 3 mol H₂, so 1 mol HCl produces 0.5 mol H₂ = 11.2 L at STP. TRUE
(2) Per 1 mole Al: 2 mol Al produces 3 mol H₂, so 1 mol Al produces 1.5 mol H₂ = 33.6 L at STP only, not regardless of T and P. FALSE
(3) Volume ratio at same T,P: 6 mol HCl : 3 mol H₂ = 2:1, so 12 L HCl : 6 L H₂. TRUE
(4) Per 1 mole Al: 1.5 mol H₂ = 33.6 L, not 67.2 L. FALSE
Option (1) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Aqueous HCl reacts with $\mathrm{MnO}_{2}(\mathrm{~s})$ to form $\mathrm{MnCl}_{2}(\mathrm{aq}), \mathrm{Cl}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(l)$. What is the weight (in g) of $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ liberated when 8.7 g of $\mathrm{MnO}_{2}(\mathrm{~s})$ is reacted with excess aqueous HCl solution?
(Given Molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{Mn}=55, \mathrm{Cl}=35.5, \mathrm{O}=16, \mathrm{H}=1$)
questions.solution:
The balanced redox equation is: $\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{MnCl}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Molar mass of MnO₂ = 55 + 32 = 87 g/mol.
Moles of MnO₂ = $\frac{8.7}{87} = 0.1$ mol.
From stoichiometry, 1 mol MnO₂ produces 1 mol Cl₂, so 0.1 mol produces 0.1 mol Cl₂.
Mass of Cl₂ = $0.1 \times 71 = 7.1$ g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
14.0 g of calcium metal is allowed to react with excess HCl at 1.0 atm pressure and 273 K. Which of the following statements is incorrect?
[Given : Molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{Ca}-40, \mathrm{Cl}-35.5, \mathrm{H}-1$]
options: The limiting reagent is calcium metal.
questions.solution:
Reaction: $Ca + 2HCl \rightarrow CaCl_2 + H_2$
Moles of Ca = $\frac{14.0}{40} = 0.35$ mol. Since HCl is in excess, Ca is limiting.
Option (1): $H_2$ evolved = 0.35 mol
Option (2): Volume of $H_2$ at STP = $0.35 \times 22.4 = 7.84$ L
Option (3): Ca is limiting reagent
Option (4): Mass of $CaCl_2 = 0.35 \times 111 = 38.85$ g, not 33.3 g
Statement (4) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 80 mL of a hydrocarbon on mixing with 264 mL of oxygen in a closed U-tube undergoes complete combustion. The residual gases after cooling to 273 K occupy 224 mL. When the system is treated with KOH solution, the volume decreases to 64 mL. The formula of the hydrocarbon is :
questions.solution:
KOH absorbs $CO_2$. Volume of $CO_2$ produced = $224 - 64 = 160$ mL
Unreacted $O_2 = 64$ mL, so $O_2$ consumed = $264 - 64 = 200$ mL
For hydrocarbon $C_xH_y$: $\frac{CO_2}{\text{Hydrocarbon}} = \frac{160}{80} = 2 \Rightarrow x = 2$
$O_2$ consumed per mole = $x + \frac{y}{4} = \frac{200}{80} = 2.5$
$2 + \frac{y}{4} = 2.5 \Rightarrow y = 2$
Hydrocarbon is $C_2H_2$

questions.q:
Butane reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water following the equation given below
$\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10}(\mathrm{~g})+\frac{13}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{~g})+5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$
If 174.0 kg of butane is mixed with 320.0 kg of $\mathrm{O}_2$, the volume of water formed in litres is ________.(Nearest integer)
[Given : (a) Molar mass of $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{H}, \mathrm{O}$ are 12, 1, $16 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively, (b) Density of water $\left.=1 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}\right]$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10}+\frac{13}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{CO}_2+5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ \\ & 3 \times 10^3 \quad 10 \times 10^3 \\ \end{aligned}$
Moles of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ formed $=\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}}=5 \times \frac{2}{13} \times 10 \times 10^3$
Then $\mathrm{w}_{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}}=\frac{10^5}{13} \times 18$
$=1.3846 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~g}$
Volume of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ will be $=138.46$ litre.
Ans. 138

An organic compound weighing 500 mg , produced 220 mg of $\mathrm{CO}_2$. on complete combustion. The percentage composition of carbon in the compound is _____ \%. (nearest integer)
(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{C}: 12, \mathrm{O}: 16$)

Correct answer is $12$

questions.q:
Mass of magnesium required to produce 220 mL of hydrogen gas at STP on reaction with excess of dil. HCl is
Given : Molar mass of Mg is $24 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$.

On complete combustion 1.0 g of an organic compound (X) gave 1.46 g of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and 0.567 g of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\). The empirical formula mass of compound \((\mathrm{X})\) is ________ g.

questions.solution:
Moles of ' C ' \(=\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{CO}_2}=\frac{1.46}{44}=0.033\)

Upon passing $0.5 \mathrm{~L}$ of $\mathrm{CO}_2(g)$ over red hot coke, the total volume of the gases increased to $700 \mathrm{~mL}$. The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{CO}_2+\mathrm{C} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO}$
Stoichoimetry ratio is $1: 2$
AT STP, $P=1 \mathrm{~atm}, T=273 \mathrm{~K}, R=0.0821$
Initial moles of $\mathrm{CO}_2 ; n\left(\mathrm{CO}_2\right.$ initial $)=\frac{P V}{R T}=\frac{1 \times 0.5}{0.0821 \times 273}=0.022 \mathrm{~mole}$
In final mixture no. of moles; $n\left(\mathrm{CO}_2 / \mathrm{CO}\right.$ mixture)

=\frac{1 \times 0.7}{0.0821 \times 273}=0.031

Increase in volume is by $=0.031-0.022=0.009$ mole of gas
Final no. of moles of $\mathrm{CO}$ i.e. $n_{\text {(CO final) }}$
\begin{aligned}
& n_{\text {(CO final) }}=2 n_{\left(\mathrm{CO}_2 \text { initial }\right)}-n_{\left(\mathrm{CO}_2\right. \text { final) }} \\
& \quad=2\left(0.022-\mathrm{n}_{\left(\mathrm{CO}_2 \text { final }\right)}\right. \\
& \left.n_{\text {(CO final) }}=0.044-2 n_{\text {(CO }} \text { final }\right) \\
& \therefore \text { Now, } n_{\text {(CO final) }}+n_{\text {(CO final) }}=0.031 \\
& n_{\left(\mathrm{CO}_2\right. \text { final) }}=0.031-n_{\text {(CO final) })} \ldots \text { (iii) }
\end{aligned}

Substituting (ii) in eq. (i)

\begin{aligned}
& n_{\text {(CO final) }}=0.044-2\left[0.031-n_{\text {(CO final) }}\right. \\
& n_{\text {(CO final) }}=0.044-0.062+2 n_{\text {(CO final })}
\end{aligned}

n_{(\mathrm{CO} \text { final) }}=0.018 \mathrm{~mol} .

Volume of $\mathrm{CO}=V=\frac{n R T}{P}=\frac{0.018 \times 0.0821 \times 273}{1}=0.40$ Litre
and volume of $\mathrm{CO}_2=0.7$ litre $-0.4$ litre $=0.3$ litre

\therefore \mathrm{CO}_2=300 \mathrm{~mL}, \mathrm{CO}=400 \mathrm{~mL}
